# Next Kanban

Next Collection board that groups report rows into columns by Column Key, with counts, work-in-progress limits and moving cards by drag and drop or keyboard. Follows the column-board pattern of task tools, but the column header carries the load: every limit slot is drawn, so a full or overloaded column is visible before any card is read. Five styles, each for a named use: Calm lanes (smart, a procurement requisition pipeline; lanes stack when the region is narrow), Ops board (bold, a facilities work-order wallboard with large counts and priority codes), Sticky wall (depth, a campaign planning workshop of paper notes that lift when moved), Due timeline (motion, contract and licence renewals grouped by due date inside each column) and Compact list (smart, a field supervisor's phone view with one column per tab; drop a card on a tab to move it). The board never writes to the database: a move fires the amc:kanban-move event and can set page items for a Dynamic Action to save it.

| | |
|---|---|
| Plug-in type | templateComponent |

| APEXlang reference | `type: plugin/nextKanban` |
| Modes | report (multiple rows) |
| Minimum APEX | 23.1 (APEXlang import: 26.1+) |
| Version | 1.0.0 |

One query row per card, already ordered by column and then by position (order by column_seq, card_seq). Map Card ID, Column Key, Column Label and Title; Column Limit (a number, the same on every row of the column) turns on the work-in-progress warning. To show an empty column, return one row for it with Card ID and Title empty. Due Date is ISO text, TO_CHAR(due_on, 'YYYY-MM-DD'). Priority accepts critical, high, medium or low; State accepts success, warning, danger, info or neutral; Tags is a | separated list. When a card is moved the region fires the custom event amc:kanban-move with detail id, from, to, index (0-based position in the target column) and fromIndex, and first sets the page items named in Card Item, From Item, To Item and Index Item, so a Dynamic Action on that custom event can run a PL/SQL process that saves the move and then refreshes the region. Without JavaScript the rows show as a plain list.

## Settings

| APEXlang setting | Builder label | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `style` | Style | selectList (`calmLanes`, `opsBoard`, `stickyWall`, `dueTimeline`, `compactList`) | yes | `calmLanes` | Design of the board; the direction is given in brackets as motion, depth, bold or smart. calmLanes [smart]: flat tinted lanes with quiet borderless cards and limit slots under each column name; the lanes stack when the region is narrow. opsBoard [bold]: a dense wallboard with large column counts, one-line cards and a solid priority code P1 to P4 (tags are not shown), and a column that goes over its limit turns red. stickyWall [depth]: paper notes tinted by priority, slightly turned, that lift off the wall while they are moved. dueTimeline [motion]: cards inside each column are ordered and grouped by Due Date into Overdue, Today, This week, Later and No date, and overdue dates pulse gently; moving up and down is off because the order comes from the date. compactList [smart]: one column at a time behind tabs with counts, for phones and narrow side regions; drop a card on a tab to move it there. |
| `cardId` | Card ID | sessionStateValue | yes |  | Primary key of the card, returned as id in the amc:kanban-move event and put in Card Item. Leave it empty (with Title empty) on a row that only makes an empty column visible. |
| `columnKey` | Column Key | sessionStateValue | yes |  | Code of the column the card is in, for example REQUESTED or IN_REVIEW. Rows with the same key form one column; columns appear in the order their first row arrives. Returned as from and to in the amc:kanban-move event. |
| `columnLabel` | Column Label | sessionStateValue | yes |  | Column name shown in the header, for example In review. The first row of each column provides it. |
| `columnLimit` | Column Limit | sessionStateValue |  |  | Work-in-progress limit of the column as a whole number, for example 4. The header draws one slot per allowed card, says At limit when full and Over limit by N when exceeded. Empty or 0 means no limit. |
| `title` | Title | sessionStateValue | yes |  | Card heading, for example PR-2291 Laptops for the Dammam branch. |
| `description` | Description | sessionStateValue |  |  | Optional one or two lines of detail. Ops board and Compact list show one line. |
| `assignee` | Assignee | sessionStateValue |  |  | Name of the person who owns the card, for example Maha Alharbi. |
| `initials` | Initials | sessionStateValue |  |  | One or two letters shown in the assignee disc, for example MA. |
| `dueDate` | Due Date | sessionStateValue |  |  | Due date as ISO text, TO_CHAR(due_on, 'YYYY-MM-DD'). It is shown in the page language and marked Overdue or Due today; Due timeline groups cards by it. |
| `priority` | Priority | sessionStateValue |  |  | critical, high, medium or low. Critical and high are shown as Urgent and High; medium and low stay quiet except in Ops board (P1 to P4) and Sticky wall (note tint). Other values render as medium. |
| `tags` | Tags | sessionStateValue |  |  | Short labels separated by \|, for example Riyadh\|IT hardware. Keep to two or three. |
| `state` | State | sessionStateValue |  |  | Health of the card: success (Done), warning (At risk), danger (Blocked), info (Waiting on others) or neutral (no label). Always shown as text, never by color alone. Unknown values render as neutral. |
| `linkUrl` | Link URL | sessionStateValue |  |  | Optional page URL that opens the card, built in SQL with apex_page.get_url. The title becomes the link. |
| `allowMove` | Allow Moving | yesNo |  | `Y` | Yes lets users move cards by dragging or with the Move button and arrow keys. No shows a read-only board. |
| `cardItem` | Card Item | text |  |  | Name of a page item, for example P10_CARD_ID, that receives the moved card's ID before amc:kanban-move fires. Use a hidden item and submit it from the Dynamic Action. |
| `fromItem` | From Item | text |  |  | Name of a page item that receives the Column Key the card left, for example P10_FROM_COLUMN. |
| `toItem` | To Item | text |  |  | Name of a page item that receives the Column Key the card was moved to, for example P10_TO_COLUMN. |
| `indexItem` | Index Item | text |  |  | Name of a page item that receives the new 0-based position of the card in its column, for example P10_POSITION. |

## Install

- **APEX 26.1+ with APEXlang:** copy `dist/apexlang/shared-components/plugins/next-kanban/` into your app's `shared-components/plugins/`, then run the apexlang skill's format, compiler-truth and runtime validate gates.
- **APEX 23.1 to 25.x (or any version, via App Builder):** import `dist/legacy/amc_next_kanban.sql` from Shared Components > Plug-ins > Import.
